text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Shipyard Van der Giessen-De Noord shares plunge 20 percent to Dfl 48,50 after last Monday's profit warning. (p1)
- Dutch wholesalers see five percent turnover growth this year. (p1)
- Chapter One, ABN Amro's rival bidder for U.S. savings bank Standard Federal, withdraws its bid. (p1)
- Coalition liberals urge for further tax cuts under next government. (p1)
- Fokker receivers looking for answer from South Korean government by Thursday on a possible takeover of bankrupt planemaker by Samsung Aerospace. (p3)
- Three private investors, led by former director of Central Planning Bureau, take five percent stake in department store chain KBB. (p3)
- Builder NBM-Amstelland's environmental arm NBM-Milieu to close its soil decontamination installation in Schiedam. (p3)
- 62 jobs have to go at food company Nestle's plant in Elst. (p3) DE VOLKSKRANT
- Banks want consumers to foot the bill for the switch from guilder to euro. (p1)
- Amsterdam stock exchange traders amazed at relentless rise in share prices. (p2)
- Russian company Tonar is suing retailer Ahold and Dutch State over Ahold's termination of cooperation agreement with Tonar. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Cabinet threatens to resign unless parliament drops its objections to routing proposed high-speed rail link through "green heart" of western conurbation. (p1)
- Finance minister Gerrit Zalm has tax windfall this year of two billion guilders. (p3)
- Machinery maker Holec in the running for British rail maintenance orders worth 50-100 million guilders. (p25)
- Dutch wholesalers' association NVG criticises EU anti-dumping policy. (p25)
TROUW
- Rabobank heads consortium launchingfund to invest in privatised businesses in Russia's southern Black Earth region. (p6)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Government needs further spending cuts to fund necessary investments in roads, environment, public transport and education, civil service think-tank warns. (p1)
- Unilever subsidiary Mora and BolsWessanen unit Favory Convenience Food mount price war in deep-freeze snacks. (p12)
